default_pack/design.purpose: Build a software artifact from a brief, name and acceptance command, as commits on the run's own branch in a git worktree: of the repository `target` names, or of a new project when it names none. Research, strategy and the design go straight to the approval gate, with no design reviewer: the design is written once to a light template (Summary, Changes, Tests), a claims check lists what it cannot confirm, and only a design with no ## Changes goes back for a rewrite (`design_review_attempts`, default 1); everything else is shown on the approval card. A scoped change (a refine, or one whose research footprint is small) skips the perspectives step, and a refine by default (`refine_design=light`) skips research and pitfalls too: its design starts from the pull request's description and diff. The builder works in a prepared clone of the last attempt (installs, setup and generate done), where it changes the code and runs the tests its change touches and the brief's own example (the full check runs beside the reviews in fork_qa); the clone's diff becomes the attempt. Every attempt — first or fix-up — runs only the tests the change touches in the self-check. The full check runs beside the three reviews, the verifier and the early asks judge in fork_qa. gate_check composes one send-back from check failures and early-asks findings without spending an attempt (`self_check_fixups` times an attempt; past that, failures stop the attempt and not-built items alone go on to the reviews, listed for the QA judge and Overwatch), a fix-up's self-check runs the last failures and what the fix-up changed within `self_check_timeout_s`, and a failure the base shares is inherited unless the brief or a correction names it. The command runs in that worktree beside the separate QA reviews (on the commit both see, running the full check beside them) and stays binding; a QA judge then reads the reviews and decides whether the build goes on or back, and Overwatch judges acceptance with an audit of the person's gate corrections as evidence (a correction given after the approval is applied to the design before the builder's next round, because every send-back to the builder goes through the corrections step, and Overwatch does not pass the change while one is unapplied); final current validation evidence is required. Only an ask, a correction, a failed health check or a critical or high defect sends the build back, and a correction Overwatch finds unmet always does; other findings are listed on the pull request as follow-ups. A judge whose verdict cannot be read is asked again once (`judge_rereads`), with no builder round. Once they pass, the branch is delivered as a pull request (into the branch its base came from, or the default branch), which the approval gate's question names first (`pr=0` keeps it local, with its pull request text in pull-request.md and finishing commands in delivery.json; `refine` updates an open one, rewriting only the sections delivery wrote in its description). When a limit stops the build (the check's, the reviews', all attempts', or refused emissions') at an applied commit with current check evidence, that commit is delivered as a draft pull request listing what is unresolved, marked [check failing] when its check fails.

cli:optimize.purpose: Search a scored mode through the terminal with profile/project defaults and explicit overrides; resume retains the saved run identity. The omit_steering option leaves graph controls and correction audits active while excluding the ledger from candidate model prompts. The val_gate option (it needs a parts manifest with a val part) evaluates as the SkillOpt strategy does: per-epoch train seeds, a candidate stays a parent only when its val score strictly beats the gate's current candidate's, the last epoch's proposals are scored, the best on val is the winner, and with a test part the final candidate's val check and the seed, best and final candidates' test scores are run and reported. With it, early_stop_patience (0, off, by default) stops after that many epochs without a better best val score, and early_stop_at_full_val once the best val score is 1.0. The train_minibatch option (0, the whole train part, by default; it needs val_gate) scores each epoch's candidates on that many train items sampled with the per-epoch seed, and the optimizer's evidence is that minibatch; val and test are not sampled. The allow_new_node_tools option (off by default) lets an agent node an edit adds run with tools; off, a new agent runs with tool_policy none and asking for tools is refused (E-new-node-tools). The allow_code_nodes option (on by default) lets an edit add a code node, an op or gate whose Python the optimizer writes, run sandboxed; off, or where the sandbox is unavailable, a new code node is refused (E-code-nodes). The fresh_evidence option (on by default; it acts with val_gate) re-scores the candidate the optimizer edits on each epoch's train sample with that epoch's seed, unless it was scored this epoch, so its evidence is fresh; its id and scores stay. The max_edits_per_proposal option (4 by default; 1 is single edits) lets one proposal bundle that many edits, applied in order as one candidate and judged once. The strategy_option option (KEY=VALUE, repeatable) adds to a profile's strategy_options, as knob adds to its knobs; a strategy option the strategy does not read, an unknown setting or a value of the wrong type is refused. The parent_picker option (empty by default) pairs a parent picker (archive, evolutionary, islands, hill_climb, map_elites) with the optimizer: the picker chooses the candidate each step edits and the optimizer writes the edits against it; population pickers are refused with val_gate. The portfolio option (off by default; prompt+pipeline, with the autoresearch optimizer) asks the model proposer each round for one prompt/knob-level and one pipeline-level candidate and evaluates both; the report counts the evaluations beyond batch_size.

examples.explanation: Preview or queue boundary pause/resume/stop/rerun controls. Recovery preserves saved routes and rejects unknown side effects or stale fingerprints; a rerun of a failed run takes acknowledge_failure once its side effects are inspected.

Acknowledge an executing, failed or paused checkpoint whose owner died: moves pending delivery markers and mismatched outputs to set-aside, writes an SHA-bound acknowledgement so recovery accepts the checkpoint.
Correct a run's check (or --setup / --generate) command: records the change in facts.json command_history, queues a rerun control with commandCorrection semantics so the spine accepts a due node.
Remove a queued control that was never applied, so it does not affect the next owner. Refuses if the control has already been applied.

Bring a finished or failed-at-deliver run's pull request up to date with main: merges current main, regenerates, re-checks and pushes, starting the owner process. Equivalent to rerun --node deliver plus resume, without needing --text, --revision or a preview.

Write a person-only completion_override into spine-status.json, allowing update_goal complete despite a non-done status. The override is bound to the current status and invocation; it is cleared when recordStatus() writes a different status.

Queue a person's skip for a check node (a runtime_evidence producer). The source 'person' is hard-coded. After queuing, resume the run with `refactory graph-control resume --run <dir> [--acknowledge-failure]`.

interfaces.chat: Unavailable as a direct chat mutation; use the documented CLI/panel route.
interfaces.panel: Graph boundary controls and recovery preview.

graph-control.purpose: Preview or queue boundary pause/resume/stop/rerun/redeliver/acknowledge/amend-command/withdraw/confirm-completion/skip controls. Recovery preserves saved routes and rejects unknown side effects or stale fingerprints; a rerun of a failed run takes acknowledge_failure once its side effects are inspected. resume --acknowledge-failure also starts an owner for a failed checkpoint. acknowledge transitions an executing or failed checkpoint whose owner died. amend-command corrects a run's setup, check or generate command. withdraw removes a stale queued control. stop on a terminal run signals the lingering owner directly. redeliver brings a finished or failed-at-deliver run up to date with main in one command. confirm-completion writes a person-only completion_override into spine-status.json, allowing update_goal complete despite a non-done status. skip queues a person's skip for a check node (a runtime_evidence producer); the source 'person' is hard-coded.

examples.explanation: Preview a scored mode’s effective optimization settings, immutable contract and worker provenance without launching a search. Set omit_steering to exclude steering from candidate model prompts without disabling correction gates or audits.

interfaces.chat: refactory action profile-resolve
interfaces.panel: Preview resolved configuration button.

profile-resolve.purpose: Preview a scored mode’s effective optimization settings, immutable contract and worker provenance without launching a search. The omit_steering option leaves graph controls and correction audits active while excluding the ledger from candidate model prompts. The allow_new_node_tools option (off by default) lets an agent node an edit adds run with tools. The fresh_evidence option (on by default; it acts with val_gate) re-scores the candidate the optimizer edits on each epoch's train sample with that epoch's seed, unless it was scored this epoch, so its evidence is fresh; its id and scores stay. The max_edits_per_proposal option (4 by default; 1 is single edits) lets one proposal bundle that many edits, applied in order as one candidate and judged once. The strategy_option option (KEY=VALUE, repeatable) adds to a profile's strategy_options, as knob adds to its knobs; a strategy option the strategy does not read, an unknown setting or a value of the wrong type is refused. The parent_picker option (empty by default) pairs a parent picker (archive, evolutionary, islands, hill_climb, map_elites) with the optimizer: the picker chooses the candidate each step edits and the optimizer writes the edits against it; population pickers are refused with val_gate. The portfolio option (off by default; prompt+pipeline, with the autoresearch optimizer) asks the model proposer each round for one prompt/knob-level and one pipeline-level candidate and evaluates both; the report counts the evaluations beyond batch_size.

examples.explanation: Optimize a scored mode in a separate process; returns a durable run ID for status. Project defaults, profile and explicit settings resolve before launch. Set omit_steering to exclude steering from candidate model prompts without disabling correction gates or audits.

interfaces.chat: refactory action start
interfaces.panel: Optimize button.

start.purpose: Optimize a scored mode in a separate process; returns a durable run ID for status. Project defaults, profile and explicit settings resolve before launch. The omit_steering option leaves graph controls and correction audits active while excluding the ledger from candidate model prompts. The val_gate option (it needs a parts manifest with a val part) evaluates as the SkillOpt strategy does: per-epoch train seeds, a candidate stays a parent only when its val score strictly beats the gate's current candidate's, the last epoch's proposals are scored, the best on val is the winner, and with a test part the final candidate's val check and the seed, best and final candidates' test scores are run and reported. With it, early_stop_patience (0, off, by default) stops after that many epochs without a better best val score, and early_stop_at_full_val once the best val score is 1.0. The train_minibatch option (0, the whole train part, by default; it needs val_gate) scores each epoch's candidates on that many train items sampled with the per-epoch seed, and the optimizer's evidence is that minibatch; val and test are not sampled. The allow_new_node_tools option (off by default) lets an agent node an edit adds run with tools; off, a new agent runs with tool_policy none and asking for tools is refused (E-new-node-tools). The allow_code_nodes option (on by default) lets an edit add a code node, an op or gate whose Python the optimizer writes, run sandboxed; off, or where the sandbox is unavailable, a new code node is refused (E-code-nodes). The fresh_evidence option (on by default; it acts with val_gate) re-scores the candidate the optimizer edits on each epoch's train sample with that epoch's seed, unless it was scored this epoch, so its evidence is fresh; its id and scores stay. The max_edits_per_proposal option (4 by default; 1 is single edits) lets one proposal bundle that many edits, applied in order as one candidate and judged once. The strategy_option option (KEY=VALUE, repeatable) adds to a profile's strategy_options, as knob adds to its knobs; a strategy option the strategy does not read, an unknown setting or a value of the wrong type is refused. The parent_picker option (empty by default) pairs a parent picker (archive, evolutionary, islands, hill_climb, map_elites) with the optimizer: the picker chooses the candidate each step edits and the optimizer writes the edits against it; population pickers are refused with val_gate. The portfolio option (off by default; prompt+pipeline, with the autoresearch optimizer) asks the model proposer each round for one prompt/knob-level and one pipeline-level candidate and evaluates both; the report counts the evaluations beyond batch_size.
